name: ESP32-P4-NANO-WIFI6-DB

usb.notes: The Type-C port goes through a CH343P to UART0 (GPIO37/38). The Type-A port is USB 2.0 High-Speed OTG on dedicated pads, not GPIOs.

verification.notes: Pins from the hardware guide's GPIO allocation table and the BSP header. CH343P on GPIO37/38 checked in the schematic. Chip revision v3 from the X suffix (datasheet table 1-1) and the BSP's ESP-IDF >= 5.5 requirement.

peripherals.notes: Shared with the display connector (GT911 touch 0x5D/0x14, backlight 0x45) and camera SCCB.
dout = P4 to codec DSDIN, din = codec ASDOUT to P4.
Active high. GPIO53 is also on the header.
Slot 0. pwr is active low. Card IO is powered from on-chip LDO channel 4. GPIO45 is also on the header.
Internal EMAC over RMII, PHY address 1. REF_CLK is a 50 MHz clock from the PHY. Optional PoE module.
Wi-Fi 6 (2.4/5 GHz) / Bluetooth 5 LE coprocessor with external antenna. Use esp_wifi_remote + esp_hosted (SDIO host). rst drives C5 CHIP_PU (low = reset). GPIO54 and GPIO6 are also on the header.

warnings: Waveshare's hardware guide says the ESP32-P4NRW32X has 16 MB of PSRAM, but the part number (and Espressif's datasheet) means 32 MB. The profile uses 32 MB. Check with `wsesp.py detect` on your board.

This board has a v3.x chip, so it needs ESP-IDF 5.5 or newer built for revision >= 3.0 (the generated sdkconfig.defaults does this). Firmware built for the older ESP32-P4-NANO (v1.x chip) does not boot on it.
GPIO35 is both the BOOT button and Ethernet RMII TXD1. Don't hold BOOT while Ethernet is running, and don't attach anything that pulls GPIO35 low at reset.
GPIO36 is a strapping pin with an external pull-up on the header. GPIO34/35 (Ethernet) and GPIO37/38 (UART0) are also strapping pins.
GPIO0/1 are on the header but wired to the 32 kHz crystal. Waveshare's docs say to remove R32/R36 before using them as GPIO.
GPIO24-27 are on the header and default to the USB 1.1 PHY functions (GPIO24/25 = USB Serial/JTAG). Reconfiguring them disables those.
Not the same board as the ESP32-P4-NANO: the coprocessor is an ESP32-C5 and GPIO45 switches SD card power.
